chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man to whom his wife entrusts her dowry, and it is less than the dowry of his other wives. He said: 'It is added to the dowry of his wives, so it does not contradict the first report, because this narration is understood to be when she entrusts it to him on the condition that he makes it equal to the dowry of his wives; so whenever he falls short of that, it is added to it. But if it is absolute, the ruling is what the first report contained, that whatever he judges is valid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a wife entrusts her dowry amount to her husband and he sets it lower than her co-wives' dowries?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Al-Istibsar* to clarify the distinction between conditional and absolute entrustment (*tafwid*) of the dowry, a key nuance in Shia jurisprudence regarding marital contracts. The Imam explains that if the wife specifies the dowry must match her co-wives', any shortfall is legally added to her share to ensure equity; however, if the entrustment is absolute, the husband's determination is final and binding. This highlights the Shia emphasis on contractual precision and the protection of the wife's financial rights within the marriage.
